description: What a valid CHARTER.md is, as data (#3481). The framework's charter helpers read their constants from here; cases[] is the conformance suite a downstream implementation of the placeholder rule runs to show it agrees.

title.description: A generation requirement only: what /charter writes on line 1 of a new CHARTER.md, title.form with {name} as the project name, and what line 1 must match. It is not an input to the filled/unfilled decision: a charter is a template only by the placeholder rule, so a filled charter with any other title is filled (cases[] filled-charter-nonconforming-title). A consumer deciding whether a charter is filled must not test the title.

codeExclusion.fenceClose: A line whose leading run (after optional whitespace) is the opening fence's character, at least as long as the opening run, closes the fence. Every line from the opening fence to its close, both included, is removed. An unclosed fence removes the rest of the document.
codeExclusion.inlineCode: Outside fences, a run of N backticks, then text (possibly empty) containing no backtick, then N backticks, form one span, matched left to right; the span is removed. Spans never cross a line.

cases.description: Braces inside an inline code span are literal content: a path convention is not a placeholder. Praxis Hub Manager getCharterStatus strips no code and reads this as Pending.

cases.description: A backtick-fenced block is removed, opening and closing lines included.
A tilde fence is removed too, and a shorter or different-character run inside it does not close it.
An unclosed fence removes the rest of the document.
A double-braced token inside a double-backtick span is literal content; one outside code is a placeholder.
Inline JSON is not a placeholder: a leading quote, digit or space does not match.
Lowercase-kebab and double-braced upper-snake tokens are both placeholders, listed in document order.
CRLF line endings are normalized before fences are found.
A filled charter in contract shape is not a template.
